statement: Regular hexagon $ABCDEF$ has area $72$. Point $M$ is the midpoint of side $\overline{CD}$. What is the area of triangle $AMF$?

choices.misconception: I split the triangle at the center $O$ of the hexagon and added triangle $OAF$ (area $12$) and triangle $OMA$ (area $6$), but forgot triangle $OFM$.
I thought any triangle with one side of the hexagon as its base and its third vertex on the opposite side must be half of the hexagon.
I found the area of the two pieces of the hexagon outside triangle $AMF$, $24 + 24$, and gave that instead.
I subtracted only triangle $ABM$, which has area $18$, from the hexagon, forgetting the piece on the other side of $\overline{FM}$.

hints: Which side of the hexagon is parallel to $\overline{AF}$?
Side $\overline{CD}$ is parallel to $\overline{AF}$, so the height of triangle $AMF$ from $M$ is the distance between these two opposite sides, wherever $M$ sits on $\overline{CD}$.

Slide $M$ to $D$; the area does not change. If $O$ is the center, segment $\overline{FO}$ splits triangle $ADF$ into triangles $OAF$ and $ODF$, and each has the same area as one of the six equilateral triangles of area $12$.

solutions.reliable: Split the hexagon into six equilateral triangles of area $12$ around its center $O$; let $s$ be the side and $h$ the height of each, so $\frac{1}{2}sh = 12$. In a regular hexagon opposite sides are parallel, so $\overline{CD} \parallel \overline{AF}$, and the distance between them is $2h$ (the hexagon is two rows of these triangles tall in that direction). Triangle $AMF$ has base $AF = s$ and height $2h$, so its area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot s \cdot 2h = 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}sh = 24$.
solutions.elegant: Because $\overline{CD} \parallel \overline{AF}$, moving $M$ along $\overline{CD}$ does not change the area of triangle $AMF$. Move it to $D$. Segment $\overline{FO}$ is a median of triangle $ADF$ (since $O$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AD}$), so it splits $ADF$ into two triangles of equal area. One of them, $OAF$, is one of the six equilateral triangles, with area $12$. So triangle $AMF$ has area $24$.
